correctness.rationale: Modal correspondence proved by separate singleton valuation witness and successor comparability case split; sparse independently distributed outgoing-row fork indicators yield Poisson mean c²/2 with comparable-fork expectation o(1); dense independent mutually missing dyads yield Poisson mean c²/2 with witnessless pair expectation o(1); middle regime uses exact fork-pair variance, Markov bound for comparable forks at small p, and missing-pair concentration at p bounded below. originality.rationale: The result is a complete two-ended quantitative validity diagram for modal weak connectedness on independently sampled directed relations, with different sparse and dense critical exponents and the same Poisson-zero law. Foundational qualitative frame correspondence, single-scale rare-subgraph Poisson methods and neighborhood graph terminology are expressly prior. Actual published-finding corpus and primary-literature searches did not locate an equivalent full probabilistic theorem; historical-priority and general rare-pattern coverage are residual risks.
residual_risks: General rare-forbidden-pattern limit theorems may imply some or all windows as specialized corollaries; no decisive general full-text comparison was identified.
Bang-Jensen 1990 full text not accessible; probabilistic coverage was not established from the abstract.

value.rationale: Weak connectedness is a standard mathematical criterion for local successor width in modal frames. The theorem supplies the full asymptotic validity phase diagram under the canonical independent-arc ensemble, including two different scaling exponents but one universal Poisson crossover, and an intermediate region of almost-sure invalidity. The exponent mismatch has a structural explanation: sparse failures are isolated fork tails, whereas dense failures cluster about one mutually missing dyad. This is a motivated global probability invariant, rather than an arbitrary finite slice or routine recomputation.
